correctness.rationale: In a spider with s length-two arms and t short leaves, an independent dominating set picks exactly one member of each (a_i,b_i). If it contains the center, it is uniquely C={c,b_i}, of cardinality s+1. Otherwise it is exactly S_X, choosing a_i on X and b_i outside X plus all t short leaves, size s+t; it dominates the center iff t>=1 or X is nonempty. Comparing sizes proves the full minimum-set classification. A token slide among S_X changes exactly one coordinate along a_i b_i, giving Q_s minus zero for t=0 or all of Q_s for t=1; the latter has precisely one extra pendant center-containing state adjacent to the zero vector. For t>=2 only C minimizes. Bipartite parity, a Hamilton path from the Gray cycle, and coordinatewise shortest-path analysis prove the claimed diameter, median and non-Hamiltonian properties. Independently enumerated minimum independent dominating sets and actual token-slide edges for all nine pairs s=3,4,5 and t=0,1,2, matching counts and graph forms. This is finite corroboration; the forced-set case analysis proves all s>=3,t>=0.
